Lemma
[Positive definite forms are coercive]

Let $V$ be finite-dimensional normed and let $q$ be bilinear with $q(v,v)>0$ for $v e 0$. Then $\{ v:q(v,v)<1\} $ is bounded; equivalently, some $c>0$ satisfies $q(v,v)\ge c|v|^2$ for all $v$.
Proof

\sketch If $V e \{ 0\} $, compactness of the unit sphere gives a minimum $c>0$ of $q(v,v)$ there. Scaling $u=v/|v|$ yields $q(v,v)\ge c|v|^2$; hence $q(v,v)<1$ implies $|v|<c^{-1/2}$. The zero space is vacuous.

□
